title: Edinburgh's top three most haunted theatres and the spirits who live there
excerpt: In a list of the UK's most spookiest theatres, Edinburgh claimed all three of the top spots and is widely recognised as one of the most haunted cities in Europe

Spooky season is here and while Halloween is typically associated with horror films and jump scares behind the screen, it turns out some of the most chilling stories are actually taking place in theatres across the UK. However, in these cases, the shows never end as the buildings themselves are haunted.

It's not unusual for Halloween to bring out curiosity in people who love the idea of seeing a ghost in real life and not just behind the screen. According to Google Trends, many internet users are currently searching for 'haunted places near me' but it turns out one of the most commonly haunted spots in the UK is a theatre.

SeatPlan founder Ben Jackson has revealed the 13 most haunted theatres in the UK with the eeriest tales and it's good news for Scots ghost hunters as it turns out the top three are all in Edinburgh.

While another 10 theatres, mostly based in England with one in Wales, also made the list, Edinburgh was the only location in Britain to be featured three times.

The Scottish Capital is widely considered one of the most haunted cities in the world due to its its dark medieval history and centuries of plague, executions and witch trials.

So it makes sense that Edinburgh's theatres are also allegedly occupied by some spooky spirits.

From an illusionist who haunts the site of his fiery death to a former night security ghost who has never stopped guarding the venue, these are the top three haunted theatres in Edinburgh.

Edinburgh Playhouse - Albert

The Edinburgh Playhouse is said to have a resident spirit known as Albert. The mysterious figure is believed to haunt the sixth level of the building.

Witnesses have previously described seeing a grey outline or a shadowy figure, companied by a sudden chill.

Theories about Albert's identity vary, with some suggesting he was a backstage worker and other stories linking him to the night security of the building.

His repeated association with the same area of the theatre has helped to solidify his reputation among Edinburgh’s many ghost stories.

Royal Lyceum Theatre, Edinburgh: The Blue Lady

Another ghost tale in Edinburgh is The Blue Lady, who is reported to be a resident of the Royal Lyceum Theatre.

While her identity remains a mystery, some claim the figure who appears in pale blue clothing in the upper gallery is actress Ellen Terry.

The former star appeared in the theatre’s opening production in 1883.

Reports have also described shadowy apparitions high above the stage, around the lighting rig, accompanied by a ringing sound.

Festival Theatre, Edinburgh: The Great Lafayette

The ghost story of the Festival Theatre in Edinburgh is known to have a tragic history.

The venue was previously known as the Empire Palace Theatre, which was the scene of a devastating fire in 1911.

The blaze broke out during a performance of a Sigmund Neuberger, a celebrated illusionist known as The Great Lafayette, who died alongside other victims backstage.

Reported ghost stories in the Festival Theatre include guests feeling sudden cold spots and seeing shadowy figures in the basement.

The spooky venue also has reports of doors opening in empty spaces, and even the sound of a lion roaring in the auditorium.

Beyond the ghost stories and terrifying tales, historic theatres are an important part of Edinburgh and the wider UK’s cultural heritage.

In the Scottish Capital, there is a core group of around 10 to 15 major year-round permanent theatres alone.

In Britain, many theatres have stood for centuries, witnessing thousands of performers, productions, and audiences, with stories and architecture that offer a unique connection to the past.
